items.prompt: Union-find (DSU) answers which two questions fast?
choices: Are a and b in the same set? / merge two sets
Shortest path between a and b
items.whyRight: Find compares roots; union links components.
whyWrong: Topo order needs a DAG DFS/Kahn.

items.prompt: With path compression + union by rank, Find is?
choices: O(log log log n) only worst forever
items.whyRight: The amortized bound is α(n), effectively constant.
whyWrong: Naive parent walks without compression can be linear.
The famous bound is stronger than stacked logs suggest in practice.

choices: Skip edges that would connect already-linked vertices (cycles)
items.whyRight: Add edges in weight order iff they join different components.
whyWrong: Dijkstra is a different MST/shortest-path approach.
Hashing weights is unnecessary for the union check.
BSTs are not Kruskal’s cycle checker.

items.prompt: Path compression does what on Find?
choices: Points nodes along the path directly at the root
Converts the structure into a heap
items.whyRight: Flatter trees make later Finds cheaper.
whyWrong: Union by rank/size handles linking policy.

items.prompt: Interview signal for DSU: problem talks about?
choices: Merging groups / connected components over time
items.whyRight: Dynamic connectivity is the DSU home turf.

choices: The smaller (or shorter) tree under the larger root
Always left id under right id with no size check
Random roots each time for fairness
items.whyRight: Keeping trees shallow preserves Find speed.
whyWrong: Id order alone does not bound height.
A single global root without care recreates a stick.
